MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY OCTOBER — TERMLY EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvesting and Post-Harvest Handling 2.3 Fish Value Addition ? (1 mark)

   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvesting and Post-Harvest Handling 2.3 Fish Value Addition .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvesting and Post-Harvest Handling 2.3 Fish Value Addition .
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvesting and Post-Harvest Handling 2.3 Fish Value Addition .

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Value Addition.

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
